question.text: Treynor Ratio differs from Sharpe Ratio in that it uses:

answer.text: Standard deviation as the risk measure
Beta (systematic risk) instead of standard deviation (total risk)
The maximum drawdown as the risk measure

explanation.text: The Logic: Treynor Ratio measures the risk premium per unit of beta (systematic risk): (Portfolio Return - Risk-free Rate) / Beta. Sharpe Ratio uses standard deviation (total risk) in the denominator instead. Sharpe is preferred for inadequately diversified portfolios; Treynor is preferred when wealth is already diversified across asset classes. The Trap: Option A is the Sharpe risk measure, not Treynor. Option C is wrong because Treynor does use a risk measure (beta). Option D (maximum drawdown) is not a component of either Sharpe or Treynor.
